branch_analysis.reason: EO 12149 section 1-204 sends unresolved regional problems to the ICC; section 1-301 assigns ICC/OMB regional-council policy, guidance and referrals, including guidance to Federal Cochairmen; section 1-303 permits ICC requests for joint staff. These are concrete additional duties under EO 12149. EO 12314 section 4(b) expressly revokes that order and section 3 locates regional-council oversight in OMB on July 22, 1981. It neither names EO 12075 nor states that the ICC is abolished. Its narrower regional-council administration is compatible with original 1-201 to 1-204 assistance, coordination and problem-solving across executive agencies and community sectors; 1-205 already preserves EOP clearance/review/decisionmaking. Thus 1981 ends the separately added duties, not every original broad command. General support, working-group power and reporting remain tied to the surviving original Council functions. EO 12407 later revokes EO 12314 on February 22, 1983 without recreating ICC or EO 12149 duties.

sources.read_method: complete official extract read; no image verification claimed
quoted_parts:
1-204. Each Council shall attempt to identify significant problems with Federal 
policies and actions and, if such problems cannot be resolved in the Region, 
refer such problems to the appropriate agencies and the Interagency Coordi­
nating Council.

1-301. The Interagency Coordinating Council, in conjunction with the Office of 
Management and Budget shall, consistent with the objectives and priorities 
established by the President, establish policy with respect to Federal Regional 
Council matters, provide guidance to the Councils, respond to their initiatives 
and seek to resolve policy issues referred to it by the Councils. The Inter­
agency Coordinating Council shall also provide policy guidance to the Federal 
Cochairmen of the Regional Action Planning Commissions on intergovernmen­
tal matters pertaining to activities undertaken by the Federal Regional Coun­
cils.

1-303. Each Agency represented on a Council shall provide, to the extent 
permitted by law, appropriate staff for common or joint interagency task 
forces as requested by the Federal Regional Council Chairman or by the 
Interagency Coordinating Council.

THE WHITE HOUSE, 
J u ly  20, 1979.

branch_analysis.not_original_clause_inventory: EO 12149 is independently sourced additional authority; its three duties are accounted for here and in contextual later_events, not mislabeled as original 1978 text.

savings_analysis.known_scope_assessment: No surviving independent ICC command found in the eight complete official EOs read. Original 1-205 preserves pre-existing EOP procedures, not a new ICC command. EO 12148 section 2-302 preserves section 1 emergency-function transfers, not section 5-210 Council membership. EO 12149 added duties are extinguished by EO 12314; its OMB functions are separately sourced to EO 12314 and are not continuing EO 12075 commands. EO 12407 then revokes EO 12314 without a revival. The identically named council in EO 12250 is expressly the Rehabilitation Act section 507 body, not the urban/regional ICC. EO 12379 contains no target-specific saving.
savings_analysis.remaining_limitation: Overall savings/residuals disposition withheld pending actual P.L.96-88 and P.L.97-35 successor-reference, transfer, abolition, savings and effective-date text. Neither an HEW name change nor creation of an HHS Office of Community Services proves an earlier end or continuation of the corresponding original seat. No independent statutory authority is assumed to be a surviving Council command.

quoted_parts:
1-205. The functions of the Council shall neither substitute for nor 
replace Executive Office of the President clearance, review and decisionmaking 
procedures.

1-301. Executive agencies shall cooperate with and assist the Council in 
performing its functions.
i-302. The Chairperson shall be responsible for providing the Council 
with such administrative services or support as may be necessary or appropri­
ate.
1-303. The Chairperson may establish working groups or subcommittees 
of the Council. The Chairman may invite representatives of nonmember agen­
cies to participate from time to time in the functions of the Council.
1-304. The Chairperson shall report to the President on the performance 
of the Council’s functions.
